proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(E_0\) for \(E_{P_{0,O}}\), put \(G_b=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}g_{b,x}\), and stack the profiled restriction maps over the finitely many strata.  All expectations below are under \(P_{0,O}\).

We first profile the PT restriction.  By \(\mathrm{def{:}restriction\text{-}maps}\),
\[
 q_{\mathrm{PT},x}=\delta_1^0(x)\mathbf 1_J-D(x),
 \qquad
 A_{\mathrm{PT}}=I_J-J^{-1}\mathbf 1_J\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Direct multiplication gives
\[
 A_{\mathrm{PT}}\mathbf 1_J
 =\mathbf 1_J-J^{-1}\mathbf 1_J(\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}\mathbf 1_J)
 =0.
 \tag{2}
\]
Therefore, along every regular path, including paths with an arbitrary derivative \(\dot\delta_1^0(x)\) of the latent treated counterfactual change,
\[
 A_{\mathrm{PT}}\dot q_{\mathrm{PT},x}
 =A_{\mathrm{PT}}\{\dot\delta_1^0(x)\mathbf 1_J-\dot D(x)\}
 =-A_{\mathrm{PT}}\dot D(x).
 \tag{3}
\]
Equations (2)--(3), \(\mathrm{def{:}restriction\text{-}maps}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\) show that the observed profiled restriction is \(-A_{\mathrm{PT}}D(x)\) and that its Riesz representer is \(R_{\mathrm{PT},x}\).  The matrix \(A_{\mathrm{PT}}\) is symmetric and idempotent, its null space is \(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1_J\}\), and hence
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm{PT}})=J-1.
 \tag{4}
\]
If \(\widetilde R_{D,x}\) denotes the vector representing the derivative of \(D(x)\), then (3) gives \(R_{\mathrm{PT},x}=-A_{\mathrm{PT}}\widetilde R_{D,x}\).  Thus
\[
 \operatorname{rank}E_0[R_{\mathrm{PT},x}R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}]
 \le \operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm{PT}})=J-1.
 \tag{5}
\]
Under the nondegeneracy condition in the statement, the left side of (5) is \(J-1\), which proves the asserted exact-rank clause.  This qualification is necessary because a matrix projector of rank \(J-1\) can act on statistically degenerate mean gradients.

We next identify the observed projections of the causal branches.  For PT, \(r_{\mathrm{PT},x}=0\) is equivalent to \(A_{\mathrm{PT}}D(x)=0\), and (4) makes this equivalent to
\[
 D(x)=c(x)\mathbf 1_J
 \quad\text{for some scalar }c(x).
 \tag{6}
\]
Every compatible PT law satisfies (6), since no anticipation in \(\mathrm{ass{:}no\text{-}anticipation}\) makes donor final changes observable and \(\mathrm{ass{:}parallel\text{-}trends}\) equates them to the treated untreated change.  Conversely, if an observed law satisfies (6), retain every observed coordinate and choose the unobserved treated-group variable \(Y_T(0)\), conditionally on \(X=x\), to have mean \(\mu_{1,T-1}(x)+c(x)\).  Before period \(T\), impose the no-anticipation equalities.  This gives a compatible full-data PT extension without changing the observed law.  Hence the observed projection of the PT branch is locally exactly the zero set of its profiled restriction.

For SC, \(\mathrm{ass{:}sc\text{-}rank}\) implies that \(B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\) is invertible in every occupied stratum.  Thus \(w(x)=\{B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\}^{-1}B(x)^{\prime}a(x)\) is unique, and
\[
 r_{\mathrm{SC},x}=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \{I_T-B(x)[B(x)^{\prime}B(x)]^{-1}B(x)^{\prime}\}a(x)=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 a(x)=B(x)w(x).
 \tag{7}
\]
The first row in (7) is \(1=\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}w(x)\).  Under no anticipation, the remaining rows are precisely the preperiod restrictions in \(\mathrm{ass{:}synthetic\text{-}mean}\).  Conversely, from an observed law satisfying (7), retain the observed coordinates and choose the unobserved treated-group \(Y_T(0)\), conditionally on \(X=x\), to have mean
\[
 \sum_{g=2}^{J+1}w_g(x)\mu_{g,T}(x).
 \tag{8}
\]
Equations (7)--(8) give a compatible full-data SC extension satisfying the final-period mean restriction.  The rank margin makes \(w(x)\) a smooth function of the observed conditional means.  Hence the observed projection of the SC branch is locally exactly the zero set of its profiled restriction.

We now prove the tangent-space equality.  If \(s\) is the score of a branch-preserving quadratic-mean differentiable submodel, differentiating \(r_{b,x}=0\) and applying \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\) yields
\[
 E_0[R_{b,x}s]=0
 \qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X.
 \tag{9}
\]
This proves one inclusion.  For the converse, use \(\mathrm{ass{:}normal\text{-}rank}\) and the retained-coordinate convention in the definition of \(R_b\) to select, throughout a neighborhood of \(P_0\), a maximal independent coordinate vector \(r_b^{\ast}\) with gradient vector \(R_b^{\ast}\).  The other displayed coordinates impose no additional local equation.  Because the coordinates of \(R_b^{\ast}\) are linearly independent in \(L^2(P_{0,O})\), there are bounded, mean-zero functions \(v_1,\ldots,v_m\) for which
\[
 M=E_0[R_b^{\ast}v^{\prime}]
 \quad\text{is nonsingular},
 \qquad v=(v_1,\ldots,v_m)^{\prime}.
 \tag{10}
\]
Indeed, the Gram matrix of \(R_b^{\ast}\) is positive definite; truncating and recentering its coordinates gives bounded functions whose cross-moment matrix converges to that Gram matrix, so a sufficiently late truncation satisfies (10).

Let \(s\) first be bounded, mean zero, and satisfy (9).  Define a finite-dimensional exponential-tilt chart by
\[
 \frac{dP_{O,\varepsilon,c}}{dP_{0,O}}(o)
 =\frac{\exp\{\varepsilon s(o)+c^{\prime}v(o)\}}
 {E_0[\exp\{\varepsilon s+c^{\prime}v\}]},
 \qquad
 F(\varepsilon,c)=r_b^{\ast}(P_{O,\varepsilon,c}).
 \tag{11}
\]
Boundedness in (11), the finite support of \(X\) and \(G\), the positive cell margins, and \(\mathrm{ass{:}fourth\text{-}moments}\) justify differentiation under every conditional mean entering \(F\).  Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\) and (9)--(10) give
\[
 F(0,0)=0,
 \qquad
 \partial_cF(0,0)=M,
 \qquad
 \partial_\varepsilon F(0,0)=E_0[R_b^{\ast}s]=0.
 \tag{12}
\]
For completeness, the needed local correction follows directly from (12).  Differentiability gives
\[
 F(\varepsilon,c)=F(\varepsilon,0)+Mc+\zeta(\varepsilon,c),
 \qquad
 \|\zeta(\varepsilon,c)\|=o(|\varepsilon|+\|c\|),
 \tag{13}
\]
with the derivative of \(\zeta\) in \(c\) arbitrarily small on a sufficiently small neighborhood.  On a ball \(\|c\|\le C|\varepsilon|\), the map
\[
 c\longmapsto-M^{-1}\{F(\varepsilon,0)+\zeta(\varepsilon,c)\}
 \tag{14}
\]
is then a contraction of that ball into itself.  Its fixed point \(c(\varepsilon)\) satisfies \(F(\varepsilon,c(\varepsilon))=0\).  Since the last equality in (12) gives \(F(\varepsilon,0)=o(\varepsilon)\), equations (13)--(14) also give
\[
 c(0)=0,
 \qquad
 c(\varepsilon)=o(\varepsilon).
 \tag{15}
\]
Consequently the corrected path in (11) has score \(s\).  Its full profiled restriction vanishes by the locally fixed maximal coordinate system, and the extensions constructed in (6)--(8) lift it to a full-data path in branch \(b\).  The fixed interiority margins ensure that a sufficiently short segment of this path remains in the stated branch model.

Now let \(s\in\mathcal H_{P_0}\) satisfy (9), without boundedness.  Let \(\widetilde s_k\) be its truncation at level \(k\), recentered to have mean zero, and put
\[
 s_k=\widetilde s_k-v^{\prime}M^{-1}E_0[R_b^{\ast}\widetilde s_k].
 \tag{16}
\]
Each \(s_k\) is bounded and mean zero, (10) gives \(E_0[R_b^{\ast}s_k]=0\), and Cauchy--Schwarz plus \(\widetilde s_k\to s\) in \(L^2(P_{0,O})\) gives
\[
 E_0[R_b^{\ast}\widetilde s_k]\longrightarrow E_0[R_b^{\ast}s]=0,
 \qquad
 \|s_k-s\|_{P_0,2}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{17}
\]
The bounded case puts every \(s_k\) in the branch tangent set, and \(\mathrm{def{:}branch\text{-}tangents}\) takes its \(L^2\)-closure.  Combining (9) and (17) proves
\[
 \mathcal T_b(P_0)
 =\{s\in\mathcal H_{P_0}:E_0[R_{b,x}s]=0
       \text{ for every }x\in\mathcal X\}.
 \tag{18}
\]

There are finitely many retained normals, so elementary orthogonal-complement algebra applied to (18) gives
\[
 \mathcal T_b(P_0)^{\perp}
 =\operatorname{span}\{R_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X\}.
 \tag{19}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\), \(E_0[G_bs]=\dot\theta_b(s)\) for every unrestricted score.  Hence \(\mathrm{def{:}influence\text{-}classes}\) and (18)--(19) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal I_b(P_0)
 &=\{\phi\in\mathcal H_{P_0}:E_0[(\phi-G_b)s]=0
       \text{ for every }s\in\mathcal T_b(P_0)\}\\
 &=G_b+\mathcal T_b(P_0)^{\perp}
 =G_b+\operatorname{span}\{R_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X\}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{20}
\]

Finally, let
\[
 \Gamma_b=E_0[R_bR_b^{\prime}],
 \qquad
 u_b=E_0[R_bG_b].
 \tag{21}
\]
If \(c\in\ker(\Gamma_b)\), then \(E_0[(c^{\prime}R_b)^2]=0\), so \(c^{\prime}R_b=0\) almost surely and \(c^{\prime}u_b=0\).  Thus \(u_b\in\operatorname{range}(\Gamma_b)\).  The function \(R_b^{\prime}\Gamma_b^{\dagger}u_b\) is therefore the orthogonal projection of \(G_b\) onto the normal span.  For every coefficient vector \(a\), Pythagoras gives
\[
 \|G_b+R_b^{\prime}a\|_{P_0,2}^2
 =\|G_b-R_b^{\prime}\Gamma_b^{\dagger}u_b\|_{P_0,2}^2
 +(a+\Gamma_b^{\dagger}u_b)^{\prime}
   \Gamma_b(a+\Gamma_b^{\dagger}u_b).
 \tag{22}
\]
The second term is nonnegative.  Minimizing (22) over the affine class (20) proves
\[
 \phi_b
 =\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}g_{b,x}
 -R_b^{\prime}\{E_0[R_bR_b^{\prime}]\}^{\dagger}
 E_0\!\left[R_b\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}g_{b,x}\right].
 \tag{23}
\]
Because (23) is the Hilbert-space projection itself, adding or deleting redundant displayed rows changes coefficient coordinates but not the represented function.

The preceding argument is pointwise and would apply at a branch-interior law \(P\in\mathcal M_b\) if the corresponding profiled restriction-gradient rank were locally constant at that \(P\).  The frozen condition \(\mathrm{ass{:}normal\text{-}rank}\), however, is stated only at the intersection center \(P_0\).  Accordingly, (18)--(23) establish the formal claim at every such \(P_0\) without silently imposing a new branchwise rank assumption.

proposed.statement: At every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\) satisfying the displayed rank conditions, profiling the \(J\)-coordinate map \(q_{\mathrm{PT},x}=\delta_1^0(x)\mathbf 1_J-D(x)\) over the unrestricted path of \(\delta_1^0(x)\) yields the observed normal \(R_{\mathrm{PT},x}\) for \(-A_{\mathrm{PT}}D(x)\). Its displayed coordinates have Gram rank at most \(J-1\), and the rank is exactly \(J-1\) whenever \(E_{P_{0,O}}[R_{\mathrm{PT},x}R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}]\) has rank \(J-1\). For either branch, \(\mathcal T_b(P_0)=\{s\in\mathcal H_{P_0}:E_{P_{0,O}}[R_{b,x}s]=0\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal X\}\) and \(\mathcal I_b(P_0)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}g_{b,x}+\operatorname{span}\{R_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X\}\). Consequently, \(\phi_b=\sum_x g_{b,x}-R_b^{\prime}\{E_{P_{0,O}}[R_bR_b^{\prime}]\}^{\dagger}E_{P_{0,O}}[R_b\sum_xg_{b,x}]\), with redundant PT and SC rows handled by the Moore--Penrose inverse.

prose_updates.tldr: Short-panel ATT identification remains valid when either conditional parallel trends or a uniquely identified full-rank group-level synthetic-control mean restriction holds. At an intersection law, profiling the latent PT counterfactual change exposes two affine influence classes whose intersection yields a computable union convolution bound. The equal-share three-group witness has \(V_{\mathrm{PT}}=42/5\), \(V_{\mathrm{SC}}=1625/184\), and \(V_U=39/4\), with respective union costs \(27/20\) and \(169/184\). The adaptation frontier is positive only sequencewise: along each fixed root-\(n\) branch sequence the active-chart score continues at \(L^2(P_{n,O})\) distance \(O(n^{-1/2})\), with a sequence-dependent constant. Uniform one-step and multiplier attainment over the frozen sequence class is false because finite-coordinate splicing can assign distinct admissible chart labels to the same observed law.

project_justification.fill: The project profiles the PT restriction, characterizes both branch influence faces, computes their minimum-norm intersection by finite covariance-weighted programs, gives observable simultaneous and one-sided adaptation tests, and supplies a strict quantitative three-group witness. It also resolves the attainment frontier: branch-valid score continuation survives along every fixed local sequence, but the frozen class cannot support one estimator with a uniform asymptotic-linear or multiplier guarantee. A positive uniform theorem would require a genuinely common local neighborhood, common score and remainder bounds, and exclusion of arbitrary finite-coordinate replacements.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite-cell probabilities and group-time means make every profiled normal and covariance program computable. Fixed-coordinate plug-in charts admit a sequencewise \(O(n^{-1/2})\) \(L^2(P_{n,O})\) continuation along each fixed branch-local sequence, where the constant may depend on that sequence. The frozen sequence class does not authorize a uniformly valid data-driven branch selection, one-step estimator, variance estimator, or multiplier interval.

prose_updates.related_work: SunXieZhang2025 is the identification anchor. Its synthetic-control hypothesis uses one time-invariant, covariate-indexed group-weight vector for all untreated period means, exactly as in \(\mathrm{ass{:}synthetic\text{-}mean}\). The intercept row of \(B(x)\) imposes \(\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}w(x)=1\). Subtracting a reference-donor column from the other donor columns shows that \(\operatorname{rank}B(x)=J\) is equivalent to invertibility of the published reference-difference matrix \(M(x)^{\prime}M(x)\). Finite covariate support together with uniform interior cell, overlap, moment, and rank margins makes the present class a regular finite-support subclass of that published model. Therefore lower bounds and impossibility results apply to every estimator regular on the broader published union by restriction to this subclass, while sharpness is claimed only locally on the stated full-rank subclass. SunXieZhang2025, Theorems 2--4, supplies separate branchwise limit and multiplier laws; it does not supply a uniform law across the frozen branch-switching sequence class. ChenSantAnnaXie2025 supplies covariance-optimal PT weighting, while the present analysis profiles all treated-versus-donor equalities before intersecting the PT and SC influence faces. TchetgenTchetgenRobinsRotnitzky2010 studies a different finite-support union problem. SantAnnaZhao2020 supplies the single-donor panel-DiD benchmark. NeweyRobins2018 and DukesVansteelandtWhitney2024 motivate cross-fit and branchwise remainder control, but neither excludes finite-coordinate replacement; accordingly they support the sequencewise continuation, not an affirmative uniform theorem. RummoEtAl2026 and the Alaska application in SunXieZhang2025 are the motivating empirical consumers.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The union bound is local and regular at an intersection law with fixed overlap, support, moment, rank, and spectral margins. Sharpness is not claimed at SC rank failure, vanishing overlap, changing covariate support, covariance degeneracy, or on the broader published model away from this finite-support full-rank subclass. The sequencewise chart continuation is not uniform: its constant may depend on the fixed sequence, and the frozen class permits finite-coordinate replacements that preclude a common estimator expansion and multiplier coupling.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved deliverables are branchwise tangent-normal forms at regular intersection centers, the finite-program union convolution envelope, simultaneous and one-sided oracle-adaptation criteria, the strict three-group constants \(V_{\mathrm{PT}}=42/5\), \(V_{\mathrm{SC}}=1625/184\), and \(V_U=39/4\), and the single-donor reduction. A branch-valid active-chart score also continues along every fixed root-\(n\) sequence at \(O(n^{-1/2})\) \(L^2(P_{n,O})\) distance, with a sequence-dependent constant. Uniform asymptotic linearity, variance consistency, branch coupling, and multiplier coverage over the frozen sequence class are false by finite-coordinate splicing. A positive uniform result would need a common neighborhood, common score and remainder bounds, and a sequence class excluding finite-coordinate replacement. Lower-bound and impossibility conclusions transfer to estimators regular on the broader Sun--Xie--Zhang union by subclass restriction; local sharpness remains limited to the stated full-rank finite-support class.

proofs.proof_tex:
There is one stratum, and all three group probabilities equal \(1/3\), so the cell-mass and overlap assumptions hold because \(\kappa_0<1\) and \(\epsilon_0<1/3\). No anticipation holds by construction. The three untreated final changes are all zero. Hence the conditional PT assumption holds and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}restriction\text{-}maps}\) gives
\[
 D=(0,0)^{\prime},\qquad
 \delta_1^0=0,\qquad
 q_{\mathrm{PT}}=\delta_1^0\mathbf 1_2-D=(0,0)^{\prime}.
 \tag{1}
\]
The two donor columns of the preperiod matrix and the treated target are
\[
 B=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\-1&1\\-2&2\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 a=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 B^{\prime}B=\begin{pmatrix}6&-4\\-4&6\end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{2}
\]
The eigenvalues of \(B^{\prime}B\) are \(2\) and \(10\). Thus the SC rank assumption holds because \(\kappa_0<1\), and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}branch\text{-}functionals}\) may divide by this matrix. Solving \(Bw=a\) gives the unique weights \(w=(1/2,1/2)^{\prime}\). They reproduce the treated untreated mean in all three periods, which verifies the synthetic-mean assumption. Together with the assumed fourth-moment envelope, (1)--(2) prove \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_I\). The fourth-moment qualification is necessary: in the displayed Rademacher construction the largest untreated/control fourth moment is \(68\), while the treated observed final fourth moment is \((\tau^{\star})^4+6(\tau^{\star})^2+1\), so an arbitrary positive \(M_4\) need not dominate them.

For \(g=1,2,3\) and \(t=1,2,3\), define
\[
 z_{g,t}=3\mathbf 1\{G=g\}\varepsilon_{g,t}.
\]
This is the influence function of the corresponding cell mean. Independence and centering of the Rademacher innovations make the nine variables \(z_{g,t}\) pairwise orthogonal. Since \(P(G=g)=1/3\), their variances, ordered by time within groups, are
\[
 (3,3,3),\qquad (3,3/2,3/2),\qquad (6,6,6).
 \tag{3}
\]
In particular, the donor final-change influence functions have variances \(3\) and \(12\). The PT normal changes the donor weights while preserving their sum. Writing the weights as \((v,1-v)\), the part of the PT variance affected by this choice is
\[
 3v^2+12(1-v)^2.
\]
Its first derivative is \(30v-24\), and its second derivative is \(30>0\). Therefore the unique PT-efficient weights are \((4/5,1/5)\). The treated-change contribution is \(3+3=6\), so
\[
 V_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})
 =6+3(4/5)^2+12(1/5)^2
 =\frac{42}{5}.
 \tag{4}
\]
The PT restriction contrast has variance \(3+12=15>0\), while \(A_{\mathrm{PT}}\) has matrix rank one. Hence its profiled statistical normal has rank one.

We next compute the SC face. A vector orthogonal to both columns of \(B\) is \(u=(0,-2,1)^{\prime}\), with \(u^{\prime}u=5\). At the restriction, differentiating the full-rank least-squares formula for \(w\) gives
\[
 dw=(B^{\prime}B)^{-1}B^{\prime}(da-dB\,w),\qquad
 -(-2,2)dw=(0,-2/5,-4/5)(da-dB\,w).
 \tag{5}
\]
Thus the unrestricted SC gradient has coefficients, by group and time,
\[
 (-2/5,-4/5,1),\qquad
 (1/5,2/5,-1/2),\qquad
 (1/5,2/5,-1/2).
 \tag{6}
\]
Normalize the single SC normal as
\[
 \rho=u^{\prime}(da-dB\,w).
\]
Adding \(\beta\rho\) to (6), orthogonality in (3) makes its preperiod variance
\[
\begin{aligned}
 Q(\beta)
 &=3(-2/5-2\beta)^2+3(-4/5+\beta)^2
   +3(1/5+\beta)^2+\frac32(2/5-\beta/2)^2\\
 &\quad+6(1/5+\beta)^2+6(2/5-\beta/2)^2\\
 &=\frac{207}{8}\beta^2+\frac35\beta+\frac{99}{25}.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{7}
\]
Since the quadratic coefficient is positive, its unique minimizer is \(\beta^{\mathrm{or}}=-4/345\), and substitution gives \(\min_{\beta}Q(\beta)=91/23\). The final-period variance in (6) is \(3+(3/2)/4+6/4=39/8\). Consequently
\[
 V_{\mathrm{SC}}(P^{\star})
 =\frac{39}{8}+\frac{91}{23}
 =\frac{1625}{184}.
 \tag{8}
\]

Every SC influence function has final donor coefficients \((-1/2,-1/2)\), because its restriction normals use only preperiod coordinates. Equality with a PT representative therefore forces the PT donor weights to be \((1/2,1/2)\). Matching (6) to that PT representative forces \(\beta^U=-1/5\): its treated preperiod coefficients become \((0,-1)\), each donor's become \((0,1/2)\), and its final coefficients are \((1,-1/2,-1/2)\). By Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}union\text{-}envelope}\), this common representative is the union canonical gradient. Hence
\[
 V_U(P^{\star})
 =6+3(1/2)^2+12(1/2)^2
 =\frac{39}{4}.
 \tag{9}
\]
The unequal pairs \((1/2,1/2)\ne(4/5,1/5)\) and \(-1/5\ne-4/345\) show, respectively, that the PT- and SC-oracle gradients do not lie on the other affine face. Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}oracle\text{-}adaptation\text{-}frontier}\) therefore makes both one-sided Gram discrepancies strictly positive. Direct subtraction of (4), (8), and (9) yields
\[
 V_U(P^{\star})-V_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})=\frac{27}{20}>0,\qquad
 V_U(P^{\star})-V_{\mathrm{SC}}(P^{\star})=\frac{169}{184}>0.
 \tag{10}
\]
All matrices and variances in (2)--(10) depend continuously on cell probabilities, means, and second moments while the positive eigenvalues and cell probabilities remain bounded away from zero. Strict inequalities are open conditions. Intersecting this neighborhood with \(\mathcal M_I\) and the fourth-moment envelope proves the relatively open-region assertion.

The obstruction comes from the quantifiers in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}local\text{-}union\text{-}sequences}\), not from failure of the center QP. Choose the fixed margins so that \(P^{\star}\) satisfies the moment, rank, spectral-gap, overlap, and variance conditions with strict slack. For a fixed sufficiently small \(\delta\ne0\), retain the donor means and all innovation laws of \(P^{\star}\), and replace the treated untreated mean path by
\[
 (1/2+\delta)(-1,-2,-2)+(1/2-\delta)(1,2,2)
 =(-2\delta,-4\delta,-4\delta).
 \tag{1}
\]
Give its treated final outcome the same fixed additive treatment effect as under \(P^{\star}\), and call the resulting law \(Q_\delta\). Both donor changes and the treated untreated change remain zero, so the parallel-trends assumption holds. Equation (1) is reproduced by the unique full-rank SC weights \((1/2+\delta,1/2-\delta)\), so the synthetic-mean assumption also holds. The group probabilities stay equal to \(1/3\), and the innovations stay bounded. By continuity of the finite Gram matrices, their nonzero eigenvalues, and the local-score variance, all strict support, moment, rank, spectral-gap, and variance margins continue to hold for sufficiently small \(|\delta|\). Thus \(Q_\delta\in\mathcal M_I\) and it satisfies every coordinatewise margin in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}local\text{-}union\text{-}sequences}\).

Fix an integer \(m\). Form two triangular sequences. In each sequence, set the law at index \(m\) equal to \(Q_\delta\) and the law at every other index equal to \(P^{\star}\). Give the \(m\)-th coordinate label PT in the first sequence and SC in the second; use any admissible label at every other coordinate. Each sequence belongs to \(\mathfrak L_U(P^{\star})\): after its one exceptional coordinate it is identically \(P^{\star}\), so the QMD equation holds eventually with score zero and remainder zero, and every coordinate satisfies the fixed margins. Therefore, when a supremum is taken over all sequences separately at each sample size \(m\), its \(m\)-th coordinate contains both labeled copies of the same law \(Q_\delta\). This is the finite-coordinate-splicing defect.

By Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}strict\text{-}three\text{-}group\text{-}witness}\), the common score at \(P^{\star}\) uses final donor weights \((1/2,1/2)\). Hence the PT chart extension, whose normal coefficient is frozen at \(P^{\star}\), still has final donor coefficients \((-1/2,-1/2)\) at \(Q_\delta\). An SC normal has only preperiod coordinates, whereas the unrestricted SC gradient at \(Q_\delta\) has final donor coefficients \((-1/2-\delta,-1/2+\delta)\). Thus, for
\[
 \Delta_\delta(O)
 =\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{PT},P^{\star})(O)
  -\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{SC},P^{\star})(O),
\]
the final-innovation component is \(\delta(z_{2,3}-z_{3,3})\). The remaining components involve innovations at other group-period coordinates. Independence of all innovations makes those components orthogonal to the final component. The variance list (3) in the witness proof gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]
 &\ge \delta^2\{\operatorname{Var}_{Q_\delta}(z_{2,3})
                  +\operatorname{Var}_{Q_\delta}(z_{3,3})\}\\
 &=\delta^2\left(\frac32+6\right)
 =\frac{15}{2}\delta^2>0.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{2}
\]
Both chart extensions are mean-zero influence functions, so \(E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta]=0\).

Suppose, contrary to the claim, that one estimator had the requested asymptotic-linear expansion uniformly over the frozen sequence class and its admissible labels. Apply that expansion at sample size \(m\) to the two spliced sequences. Their left sides are identical because their \(m\)-th data law and their causal target are both the same \(Q_\delta\). Subtracting the two expansions would force
\[
 m^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^m\Delta_\delta(O_i)=o_{Q_\delta}(1)
 \tag{3}
\]
uniformly as \(m\to\infty\). By iid sampling and the preceding centering, the variance of the left side of (3) is exactly \(E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]\), which is bounded below by \((15/2)\delta^2\) for every \(m\). Moreover, \(\Delta_\delta\) is a bounded linear combination of the Rademacher innovations. The fourth moments of the normalized sums in (3) are therefore uniformly bounded. If (3) converged in probability to zero, uniform integrability of its squares would force its variance to converge to zero, contradicting (2).

Thus no estimator can satisfy the requested uniform asymptotic-linear expansion. Since that expansion is one conjunct of the proposed four-part construction, the full affirmative conclusion, including variance consistency and multiplier coverage tied to it, is impossible under the frozen class. The argument does not contradict the sequencewise chart continuation result: it shows precisely that a positive uniform theorem additionally needs a single uniformly quantified neighborhood, common bounds on QMD scores and remainders, and a ban on arbitrary finite-coordinate replacements.
